title: Common v1
description: Shared object and scalar definitions for the AI Transaction Authorization Infrastructure /v1 contract. Referenced by authorize-request, decision, and error schemas.

MonetaryAmount.description: A monetary amount as a canonical decimal STRING, not a JSON number. Money is represented as a string to preserve exact precision and to give the Ed25519 decision canonicalization a single, stable textual form (JSON floats have no canonical serialization). Format: optional leading minus, integer part, optional fractional part. No thousands separators, no currency symbol, no exponent. The currency is carried separately. Example: "5000.00".

Jurisdiction.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (uppercase, 2 letters) naming the jurisdiction the transaction is evaluated under.

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC (trailing 'Z'). Must be an explicit, fully-qualified instant so it canonicalizes identically everywhere.

ULID.description: ULID — 26-character Crockford base32, lexicographically sortable. Used for decision_id.

Target.description: The counterparty / resource the action is directed at (e.g. the vendor being paid).

type.description: Kind of target. Constrained enum so policy predicates can match on it deterministically.

id.description: Stable identifier of the target within its type (e.g. a vendor id in the customer's system).

Counter.description: One accumulator reading injected by the orchestrator (e.g. a budget window's spend-to-date). Predicates read these values from the request — they NEVER query Redis/Postgres/network themselves. This is what makes budget/velocity decisions deterministic and replayable (ROADMAP A#7, A#3).

id.description: Identifier of the budget/counter this reading is for (matches the rule_id of the budget predicate that consumes it).

window.description: The accumulation window this reading covers.

window_key.description: Concrete window instance the reading belongs to (e.g. the calendar month). Present so a replay pins the exact window. Optional for rolling windows.

spend_to_date.description: Amount already committed against this counter for the window, as of `as_of` (see CounterSnapshot).

CounterSnapshot.description: Point-in-time accumulator state injected by the orchestrator as an EXPLICIT decision input. Because it is part of the request vector, `(request, policy_version, evaluated_at, counter_snapshot)` fully determines the decision and any decision is byte-for-byte replayable. Absent/empty when no stateful predicate applies.

as_of.description: The instant the counter readings were taken. Distinct from `evaluated_at`; recorded so replays are exact.

counters.description: Zero or more counter readings. Empty array = no stateful state was needed.

PredicateResult.description: Outcome of a single predicate. SATISFIED/DENIED/REVIEW are the deterministic local outcomes; UNAVAILABLE marks an enriched predicate that could not complete (its declared fail-mode then governs the combined verdict — never a fabricated SATISFIED). See TRD §5, §21.

MatchedRule.description: One rule that participated in the decision, with the exact numbers that drove it — this is what a policy owner hands an auditor (TRD §7).

rule_id.description: Identifier of the rule within the policy version.

type.description: Predicate type that produced this result. The six local types plus the stateful/enriched types.

detail.description: Human-readable, number-bearing explanation of why this rule produced its result.

evidence.description: Machine-readable evidence: the concrete values the predicate used. Free-form per predicate type.

Obligation.description: A condition the caller MUST honor for the verdict to hold (e.g. step-up approval, capture within TTL, enrichment was skipped). Empty on a clean APPROVE.

Signature.description: ASYMMETRIC (Ed25519) signature over the Decision. This is the audit receipt: customers AND third parties (auditors, regulators) verify it against the PUBLISHED public key without holding any secret. It is NOT the HMAC used for request authentication — that is a separate, symmetric concern carried in request headers (see the OpenAPI security scheme). HMAC here would let any key-holder forge our decisions and is forbidden (ROADMAP A#1, TRD §11).

algorithm.description: Signature algorithm. Fixed to Ed25519 for /v1.

key_id.description: Identifier of the signing key. Enables rotation: an old decision verifies against the public key named here. Resolve via GET /v1/keys/public (JWKS-style).

value.description: The Ed25519 signature over the canonical decision bytes, base64url (unpadded).

canonicalization.description: Identifier of the canonicalization scheme used to derive the signed bytes, so third parties reproduce it exactly. See /docs/decision-canonicalization.md.
